column5: Description

As Taxidermy Tinker you can create strange, animated hybrid creatures and eerie sculptures using preserved animals, bones, and mechanical parts. Your works are often bizarre and unsettling, but not alive. You require organic materials and simple mechanisms, but your creations are short-lived and dependent on available resources. You have problems working with human bodies, or any other materials too distant from 'animal' definition. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

As Tinker specialized in Bulbs and Light Sources, you can create exotic illumination devices that produce mesmerizing and unusual effects, such as cooling, color-shifting, X-ray vision, projecting illusions, literal black light, etc. Think of Bakuda, but with bulbs, less destructive and energy intensive effects. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a Tinker specializing in Mirrors and Reflection. You can create devices to reflect and mirror various effects. For example, you can create a shield capable of nearly perfect reflection of kinetic energy attempting to break through it, or a hologram projector capable of producing a temporarily physical simulacrum of another person under your control. You have all the usual limitations of a Tinker.

You are a Tinker focused on countering the works of other Tinkers. You excel at in-depth analysis of the functions and workings of other Tinker-made devices, along with creating the necessary tools to do so. However, your main focus is on creating devices to counter other Tinkertech. You can also create counters to your own creations, but doing so has 'inbreeding' effects - making the counters worse and more dangerous with each generation if you use your own work as inspiration. 

Unfortunately, you need to observe and research the works of other Tinkers to create anything, though you can still produce most basic tools and sensors within your specialization. Fortunately, you are still free to use counter-devices in any way you want; even if using them for purposes to different than their primary function is less efficient and, in some cases, can complicate maintenance. You can use this power to counter mundane tech, but its effectiveness is inversely proportional to your understanding of the targeted technology, and it generally works less well on non-Tinkertech. Your usual Tinker limitations are slightly lifted. Advice: target eldritch and alien technology.

You can create specialized machines and devices for the refinement of materials and the creation of simple components. They are easy to automate but are very focused on a single task or narrow application. For example, a small furnace that is extremely good at refining copper from scraps and ore, turning it into high-purity ingots, but it doesn't work on any other metal. You need different machine for doing something else. They are also designed to be low-scale, producing small batches of product. You don't really scale up. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You specialize in the creation of devices, tools, and items from the Neolithic Age and inspired by it. Your material requirements are relatively low and contain a lot of natural, raw materials. Your creations are unusually high quality; they are much more efficient and functional than expected from such seemingly primitive objects. You are capable of creation of non-tinkertech Neolithic items of high quality, but they just very good mundane things. Your usual Tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker specializing in the creation of Bottled Superpowers. You can create various serums, elixirs, mutagens, and fantastic concoctions to grant supernatural, scientific, eldritch, or any other type of superpower to other people. They can have vastly different sources, methods of operation, and ways of integration. However, all Bottled Superpowers are somewhat random; it's hard to create powerful ones, and some methodologies might cause usual tinker problems in the created powers (such as the need for special maintenance, instability over time, etc.). 

Your tinker restrictions are partly lifted, depending on the kind of Bottled Superpowers you are making and how or to whom you want to apply them. Advice: don't mix too many powers in one subject; use extensive human trials to get rid of some problematic kinks of your product.

Your theme and specialty are rather odd - Pseudoscience. Your creations are inspired by and function like various pseudoscientific devices, using the logic and 'knowledge' of different forms of pseudoscience. These devices are perfectly functional for what you create them for, but they are rather weird and make even less sense than usual Tinketech. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a tinker focused on the creation of 'mundane' devices, such as microwaves, freezers, toasters, and similar items. The things you make have the same functionality as their usual non-tinkertech variants, but extended, more efficient and more powerful. You can also attach some exaggerated upgrades to these basic functions if they are thematic - for example, a freezer that can keep perishable items in stasis, or a vacuum capable of absurd levels of suction. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

As a tinker specialized in fictional metals, you can synthesize such wondrous materials and produce simple objects made from them. You can create tools to actually work with these materials. It is possible for you to create a specific type of mithril, for instance. However, you must draw your inspiration from a particular work of fiction. Some materials are harder to make and use than others, some are more powerful, and some are closer to the original source of inspiration. The intangible value and theme of the fictional work greatly affect the results of your tinkering, as well as depth and quantity of information given about the metal. Your usual tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker focused on Firearms and Bullets. You can create guns and ammunition with ridiculous functions and effects, as long as they stay within the concept of 'firearm.' You cannot make pure laser weapons or plasma cannons, for instance. But a machine gun with homing rocket bullets? That is possible! Think of Bakuda, but with bullets and guns instead of bombs. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a tinker specialized in the creation of attachments for other devices. You should research and focus on a specific technological item to start building, testing and improving various add-ons for it, which can extend, deepen, or otherwise upgrade the main or secondary functions of the object. Things like an unusually efficient silencer for your pistol or perhaps a battery attachment to extend your force field charge. However, everything you create must be attached to and be a derivative of another device. Your understanding of the functions of the targeted item is very helpful. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a tinker able to create devices that reproduce and simulate various 'psychic' effects. Drawing inspiration from fiction, as well as actual supernatural and magical effects, will help you a lot. However, there is always some tradeoff in using these devices - some kind of mental cost. You can create a small device to achieve telekinetic flight, but at the cost of 4% of your maximum focus while the device is equipped. Or maybe you want to set things on fire with your gaze, but at the cost of permanently burning your own memories in quantities proportional to the complexity and power of the spontaneous combustion you are trying to achieve. Or you might literally spend your 'social battery' to fuel people-targeting psychometry. There is always a tradeoff - always a cost. At least, these devices are much less dangerous when used by you. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

This Tinker ability is all about working with the Essence and Aspects of physical objects and energy. You can build tools to decipher what conceptual components the targeted phenomenon contains, then create a device or method to extract a few highly expressed aspects from the object in the form of essences, and eventually figure out how to apply this essence to other objects. It is very research-intensive and requires one to focus on specific objects, aspects, and use cases each time. However, it allows you to create objects with bizarre properties using relatively mundane items as a source of essence. You can detect, isolate, extract, and eventually apply something like the 'toxicity' aspect from radiation to another device or material. Your usual tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

Your tinker ability is focused on the creation of various sweets to achieve your goals. It contains three broad subcategories of things you are good at: Shaping, Boost and Minions. The first is candy-material science, used to create tools, mechanisms, and devices from sweets with exotic properties. Boost is all about creating sweets that bestow positive or negative effects - temporarily (or permanently, if you try really hard) - on a target. Minions is all about creating sweets golems, animated and life-like creatures to help you with work or fighting. All your creations are technically edible. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

Your tinker ability is all about producing and folding paper to achieve your goals. It contains three narrow subcategories of things you are good at: Origami, Papermaking, and Scribbling. Origami is all about folding paper into efficient, useful shapes, and it can be used on other materials as well, but it becomes less effective the further the targeted matter is from the type of paper. Papermaking is focused on creating specialized papers for your work: bulletproof paper, hydrophobic paper, fire-resistant paper, etc. Scribbling is a more exotic craft involving inscribing patterns and text on paper to infuse it with unique added properties or to program it to do something (like folding in a specific way with a trigger condition attached). You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

Your tinker power is about the creation of 'poison' darts and pneumatic delivery systems. You can make darts of bizarre designs and imbued with interesting effects. They can be lethal or non-lethal, positive or negative, or serve some other utility (like tracking). But all these effects are chemically based. The other part is delivery systems - blowguns and similiar devices of various designs and levels of sophistication. However, they all use pneumatics to shoot the darts. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

For 24 hours, you gain a random tinkertech blueprint to work on. After 24 hours pass, the new blueprint you can build appears, and the old one disappears. You need to finish your current fixation project to save the blueprint and be able to build it again. If you cannot finish your current blueprint, all completed parts will be converted into inspiration to modify your previously saved blueprints, thematically related to the unfinished creation. You can finish a blueprint by cutting corners, but the saved blueprint will always be of a device you actually completed at the end of the current 24-hour cycle. So if you build crappy version - you get crappy blueprint. Your state of mind, levels of stress and living situation slightly affect what kind of blueprints you gain. Usually you gain blueprints, which are technically possible for your to finish in 24 hours, but not always. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

On normal days, your tinker power is very good at making simple and robust (by tinkertech standards) tools and stockpiling special materials. But you accumulate charge in this state (which has an upper limit), which you can spend to enter a special kind of fugue. In this state, you turn temporarily schizophrenic and experience heavy hallucinations. What you experience in this state determines what you will build using the materials and tools around you. This fugue is extremely efficient at making you build things, even from subpar materials. It can last up to 48 hours (maximum charge) or until you lose consciousness due to stress and fatigue. In the end, you have some useful and bizarre tinkertech device (or several) with a general idea of what it does, but you need to actually research and test it to figure out the details of maintenance and any special quirks of the created item. The state of your psyche greatly affects the products. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You can build things out of carbon extremely well. This is your main material. For instance, you can figure out a way to create a fully functional smartphone, which is made of 98% carbon. Carbon metamaterials, nanostructures, and other exotic applications of the element are your bread and butter. However, you are still limited by what is hypothetically possible, and you need to find inspiration for devices in the outside world and the technology around you. This is a methodology type of tinker power. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

Your tinker ability is uniquely centered around the concept of retrofitting - transforming and upgrading existing devices, structures, and systems into new, more advanced forms. You excel at taking old, outdated, or broken technology and infusing it with innovative modifications, turning it into something far more capable than its original design. Whether it's retrofitting a simple machine to handle complex tasks, upgrading a worn-out device with cutting-edge components, or repurposing old technology for modern use, you thrive on creatively reimagining the potential of what already exists. Your expertise lies in customizing and enhancing rather than inventing from scratch. However, your retrofitting process often results in devices that are unpredictable or temperamental - sometimes working flawlessly, other times malfunctioning in unexpected ways. This can lead to surprising outcomes. The more outdated and old the technology you are working with, the more efficient this ability is. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

Your tinker power revolves around the concept of Escalation. It allows you to push existing devices and systems beyond their original limits, increasing their power, complexity, and unpredictability. While you can turn simple gadgets into formidable or unstoppable creations, your escalations often cause unpredictable ripple effects in the environment, making your inventions prone to instability or chaos (you are less affected personally). The more pressure is applied from outside, the faster and more effectively your Escalation potential grows and quicker it can be turned into upgrades. However, if you suddenly stop escalating the acceleration 'counter' resets, and all devices built by you begin to malfunction more often, requiring more maintenance and quickly losing their power, potential and danger. This is a methodology-type of tinker power - you need outside inspiration or devices to use as a starting point for the process. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a tinker capable of creating various perpetual motion machines. Starting from basic classic designs that actually work to produce mechanical energy, and finishing with more esoteric and fundamental approaches made functional. Although, it is generally easier for you to create machines that can generate a relatively small amount of mechanical energy for an unlimited amount of time (not counting maintenance and other tinkertech-related problems). However, if you have a device on hand, it would be easy to adapt your design to power this specific machine. You have a relatively high upper scaling limit. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

Your tinker focus is all about spiders and their derivative products. You can separate this specialty into three subcategories: Spiders, Products, and Traits. The first is about affecting the actual category of creatures labeled as 'spiders': modifying them, breeding and creating new ones, controlling them, and using them as helpers with tinkertech. The second is all about derivatives: production of various silks, custom toxins, and other spider-related physical materials. The third involves applying the properties of spiders to other things: building primitive spider-bots, creating serums to grant discount Spider-Man powers, etc. This specialty heavily relies on your conceptualization, creativity and knowledge of the theme. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

Your tinker power is focused on the creation of cloned brains in boxes. You can create copies of brains (yours or other people's), download knowledge, personality, and data into them, then put these brains into jars and force them to think up ideas and solutions for you using various mastering techniques, brainwashing and various similar methods. Completely unethical, and you must ensure from time to time that these brains won't try to betray you by booby-trapping some of their ideas. However, it is really efficient for offloading solution searching and brute-forcing creativity. This specialty doesn't let you create anything else but think-tanks and will oppose you if you try to use it to create something else (like fully functional clones). Although, it includes methods of quickly and efficiently coping results from think-tanks and implanting these ideas into your head. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

This tinker power specializes in clockwork and focuses on designing, building, and manipulating intricate mechanical devices and automata. This expertise allows you to create advanced clockwork machines, precision gears, and complex gear-driven systems. You can craft autonomous clockwork robots, intricate locks and traps, or elaborate timekeeping devices. This focus is really great at working with mechanical energy and its transformations. Methodology and possible devices to create are limited by clockwork theme. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

This tinker power specializes in dieselpunk and excels at crafting rugged, retro-futuristic machinery and industrial devices. All machinery within this focus utilizes advanced variations of chemical fuel and highly sophisticated combustion engines to achieve its goals. The use of chemical fuel and combustion is a main component of practically all your designs. Your methodology and the devices you create are limited by the dieselpunk theme. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

This tinker power specializes in solarpunk and excels at designing sustainable, eco-friendly machinery and innovative devices that harmonize with nature. All equipment within this focus relies on renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and bioenergy, combined with eco-conscious materials. The development of new devices and techniques is guided by principles of sustainability and ecological balance. Your methodology and creations are limited by the optimistic and environmentally conscious spirit of the solarpunk theme. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

This unique tinker focus lets you create 'projections' of existing objects via usage of special custom devices. They function like copies of the original device or item, possessing most of its properties and functions (while not being truly material or permanent). For example, you can create a device to project several copies of a lightsaber to use, while keeping the original one safe. Or use something like an addon for the gun to essentially have infinite bullets, using projected matter to refill the gun. 

However, all projections created this way are connected to the original and cannot exist without it. At higher levels, you might store 'memory' of the original to partially sidestep this issue, but ultimately, any projection will wear out, warp in shape and function, and eventually collapse without an intact and accessible original to pull from. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

This tinker ability draws inspiration from the furry subculture and its fictional works. You create devices connected to this theme, ranging from mundane advanced fursuits with integrated technology to complex cloned bodies hosting anthropomorphic animal designs of your own creation. Any device must maintain a clear connection to the fandom and its aesthetics. Your usual tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You can apply principles of tinkertech blackboxing to mundane devices and your other creations. You have full control over the degree of blackboxing used and its nature. It can involve simple methods to make your creations resistant to reverse engineering and research by others, or a complete tinkertech-tier blackbox, making the inner workings of the machine practically incomprehensible and impossible for outside observers. However, you need to have some sort of target to apply this tinker power. It can work with a broad variety of creations, but a heavily blackboxed device might affect long-term performance and the ability of others to maintain it in a detrimental way. Different types of targets might also introduce some side-effects to the process. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

Your tinker specialty is defying the square-cube law. You build singular pieces of equipment of immense scale: a cannon the size of a car, a building-mounted pneumatic fist, or a jetpack better suited for a mech than a man. The power output is directly proportional to their colossal size. However, these devices are inherently cumbersome to move or wear, require an equally massive power supply to function. You have all the usual limitations of a tinker.

You are a tinker who transforms refuse into remarkable technology. Your specialty thrives on the worthless, broken, and discarded - the more complete the junk, the more potent the final creation. A powerful energy rifle could be built from shattered glass, used coffee grounds, and scrapped circuit boards. However, the resulting device will always inherit the "character" of its components, possessing a tendency to malfunction, break down, or produce unexpected side effects in a manner befitting its shoddy origins. You suffer all usual Tinker limitations.

Your tinker power makes you into are a master of energy redirection. You build gear designed to absorb kinetic energy from impacts, motion, or vibration and release it in a controlled, amplified burst. This could manifest as a suit that grows stronger with every blow it takes, or a gauntlet that stores the energy from a long fall to power a devastating single punch. Your technology is cyclical and self-sustaining in combat, but requires careful management to avoid catastrophic overload. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

Your tinker specialty is manufacturing misfortune or simply out 'bad luck'. You build devices that manipulate probability within a localized area, subtly skewing chance to favor chaos and failure. Your inventions don't directly attack so much as they cause things to go terribly wrong: enemy weapons jam at the worst moment, seemingly solid ground develops a treacherous slick patch, or a crucial support beam just happens to be rotted through. It's a very subtle, Thinker-y kind of Tinkering. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

Your technology is keyed to the rhythm of life itself. You build devices that are powered by and react to biological signals: heartbeat, pulse, and circulatory flow. This allows for creations with intimate user linkages: a weapon that only fires for someone with a specific cardiac rhythm, armor that hardens when the wearer's heartbeat steadies, or a diagnostic tool that can predict a target's actions by reading their blood pressure spikes. Your tech is incredibly secure and responsive, but utterly dependent on the life force of its user. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker specialized in the creation of unnaturally efficient and versatile springs. Your genius lies in using tension and release to contain and unleash energy: not just kinetic, as you can adapt the principle to channel electrical, thermal, or even more exotic forces through carefully crafted coils and wound mechanisms. However, all your devices, no matter their function, must operate on spring-based principles and retain the general aesthetic of wound metal and tension-release systems. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker who specializes in the accelerated breeding of organisms to produce unnatural and powerful results. Your true genius lies with animals, shaping generations of creatures into living tools, weapons, or mounts with terrifying speed and efficiency. You can stretch this specialty to fungi and plants, though with diminished results. All your technology is focused on facilitating this process - incubators, genetic sequencers, growth accelerators - and your methodology demands patience, as your creations must be bred, not built, over successive generations. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker who specializes in the programming and training of hyper-efficient neural networks, each one laser-focused on a narrow field of responsibility. Your expertise extends to creating custom hardware to run these networks, including wetware - organic computing systems. You can even repurpose existing living neural matter as hardware, a method that produces superior results across your entire specialty. Whether silicon or synapse, your creations excel at their singular tasks but struggle to adapt beyond their intended purpose. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You build machines that learn by breaking and being damaged. Your devices are designed to reactively adapt to stimuli within a limited field of purpose, growing more resistant and effective the more they are challenged. They are robust and possess impressive self-repair capabilities. However, your methodology demands destruction: you must test your creations to their limits in practical situations, allowing them to be damaged or destroyed to collect crucial combat data. This data alone allows you to upgrade and refine the adaptation protocols for the next generation. True growth requires sacrifice. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker who specializes in the manipulation and creative utilization of friction. Your devices exploit the principle of surfaces rubbing against one another to produce extraordinary results. This can manifest as super-lubricants that eliminate all traction, projector fields of negative friction that send objects sliding uncontrollably, surfaces with impossible grip, or weapons that generate deadly spark projectiles through rapid abrasion. Whether calming motion or catalyzing it, your tech always comes back to the art of the drag. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker who operates at the very limits of physical possibility. Your specialty is creating components with impossible tolerances and surface finishes, machining parts so perfectly that they fundamentally alter how mechanisms behave. Friction nearly vanishes between moving parts, energy transfers with zero loss, and assembled systems operate with ghost-like silence and efficiency.

This allows for a range of devastating applications: monofilament edges that slice through matter at the molecular level, armor that distributes kinetic force across its entire surface, and projectile weapons that fire rounds with zero deviation or drop. Your devices contain no exotic energy - they are simply the most perfectly made objects that have ever existed. However, each component takes considerable time to machine, and replacing a destroyed piece means starting from raw stock again. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker who specializes in the preservation of perishable targets through an advanced form of "canning." At the peak of your ability, this extends far beyond food: you can capture and store physical phenomena themselves within sealed containers. A laser blast, a stream of fire, a kinetic impact, or even another parahuman's ongoing power effect can be caught, canned, and preserved for later release or utilization. Your workshop is filled with vacuum sealers, pressure vessels, and cryo-storage units of your own design. However, each container is single-use, and the captured phenomenon will eventually degrade if stored too long. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker who shapes matter by casting process. Your molds are perfect negatives, capturing every detail at the molecular level and reproducing it with flawless fidelity. You begin by casting reletavely mundane solids from liquids with impossible efficiency, but at the peak of your focus, more exotic transitions become possible: trapping light within crystal, freezing sound into solid form, or containing a moment of pure heat inside ceramic. Whatever you pour into your forms emerges shaped and can be used for creation of other exotic components and devices using your other skills or powers. Your usual tinkering limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker who sets things straight. Your levels and plumb lines reveal true vertical and horizontal anywhere in the universe. Your gimbals keep platforms perfectly stable regardless of external motion. Your guidance systems track targets with nigh-absolute precision. You can align mechanical components so perfectly that friction nearly vanishes between them, or align forces so precisely that they reinforce rather than cancel. Everything has a proper orientation, and you can find it. Due to the fundamental nature of your specialty, the usual tinker limitations regarding maintenance, iteration, and replication almost do not apply to your power.

You are a tinker who works with barriers that let some things through while stopping others. Your membranes can filter any mixture to perfect purity, separating compounds that shouldn't be separable. Your cell walls can maintain internal pressure against vacuum or ocean depths, keeping occupants alive in hostile environments. You design systems that breathe selectively, that feed based on need, that gradually release medicine or poison when triggered by specific environmental conditions. Your limitations as a tinker are slightly lifted.

You make things tough. Your heat treatments, quenching processes, and work-hardening techniques render metals and other materials nearly indestructible. Your case-hardening penetrates deep into structural members, your tempering eliminates brittleness without sacrificing strength, and your work-hardening can make a simple paperclip strong enough to hold up a house. You do not build new devices (not counting your tools) - you take what others have built and make it unbreakable. Your limitations as a tinker are slightly lifted.

You treat the outermost layer of things. Your coatings can make a surface harder than diamond, slicker than ice, or more absorbent than any sponge. You apply finishes that hide objects from detection, that change color or texture in response to stimuli, or that slowly release embedded compounds over centuries. You believe the soul of an object resides at its skin, and you have mastered the art of perfecting that boundary between a thing and the world. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker focused on the creation and utilization of 3D printing technology in all its forms. Your specialty lies in designing and building diverse printing setups - from microscopic precision printers to large-scale construction systems - capable of producing components and even fully fledged devices. This ability excels as a force multiplier, providing manufacturing support for your other skills and tinker powers. Your printers can work in plastics, metals, ceramics, and more exotic materials, but require time and prepared feedstock to operate. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker focused on the creation and utilization of odorous substances. Your specialty encompasses perfumes that can affect the minds of living creatures when inhaled: inducing calm, fear, attraction, confusion, or obedience. Beyond mental effects, you create chemical sensors that detect and identify scents with supernatural acuity, analytical tools that break down complex odor profiles, and devices that capture, preserve, and project scents across distances. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker focused on the creation of devices that utilize mechanical wave propagation (sound and vibration) to achieve your goals. Your specialty includes things like: focused sonic projectiles analogous to lasers, listening devices of impossible sensitivity, and resonance weapons that cause targeted materials to shake themselves apart upon impact, etc. You are limited to effects theoretically achievable through mechanical waves in matter, though your solutions are unnaturally efficient at pushing those boundaries. Every creation harnesses vibration as its core principle. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker who specializes in the decomposition of materials. Your devices can achieve things like: speeding up or slowing down the rotting process dramatically, guiding decomposition to achieve limited transmutation, or causing specific materials to decay while leaving adjacent matter untouched. Your focus works best on chemically organic materials (living or dead) allowing you to wither plants, compromise wooden structures, or age biological matter and plastics to dust. Against purely inorganic substances like refined metals, stone, or ceramics, your abilities are practically useless. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker focused on bringing dead things back and making them useful (basically your minions). Given sufficient traces, you can revive an entity through cloning, repair, or stranger means like summoning its "spirit" as a projection. The quality and longevity of your creation depend on three factors: how many times you've already revived it (diminishing returns with each iteration), the quantity and condition of its remains, and how much data you possess about the original. Your specialty defines "creature" broadly - a destroyed robot qualifies as readily as a corpse. As a sub-specialty, you excel at creating single-use devices that allow you or others to avoid or shrug off death in various ways. Your limitations as a tinker are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker whose technology embodies the 22 Major Arcana of the Tarot. Each device you build is themed around a specific card's essence - you don't create a generic weapon, but a "Judgment" device that reveals hidden truths, a "Tower" device designed for catastrophic destruction, or a "Sun" device radiating pure vitality. Your creations are as symbolic as they are functional.

You may temporarily attune any of your devices to a different Major Arcana, overwriting its native theme for a short burst of that card's power. Attuning your "Chariot" boots (willpower and control) to "The Sun" might grant a sudden surge of speed and confidence. This alignment is temporary, and the device returns to its original card after use and will break down faster. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker who specializes in technology built upon loops, self-reference, and recursive systems: holograms within holograms, fractal antennae, and feedback cycles that compound upon themselves.

Your devices grow more powerful through repeated, patterned use: a shield that strengthens with each impact it absorbs, or a scanner that gains fidelity the more times it examines the same target from varied angles.

Your signature creation is the Seed: a device that, when provided with raw materials and a suitable environment, can slowly build a copy of itself or construct more advanced pieces of your technology. Given time and resources, this allows for exponential growth of your workshop and capabilities. Your limitations as a tinker are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker who builds technology in harmonized sets. Individual components are weak or non-functional in isolation, but when combined with their intended partners, they create effects far beyond the sum of their parts. However, these sets are locked - you cannot mix components from different harmonies.

Your power forces thematic commitment. If you build a fire set, everything you create for the foreseeable future must harmonize with fire. Changing sets means abandoning your previous work and starting anew. Each set forms a complete technological ecosystem. You suffer all usual Tinker limitations.

You can only build one thing. Ever. But that one thing is the most absurdly over-engineered, hyper-specialized, and powerful device conceivable within your chosen specialty. You do not build tools - you build your Magnum Opus, then spend the rest of your career refining, upgrading, and expanding it, never dividing its focus.

Your power physically prevents you from conceptualizing or constructing any device that isn't an iteration or component of your Primary. Attempts to sketch a separate tool result in a blank mind. Your Primary becomes an extension of yourself, and you can instinctively modify it for new situations, but only by permanently reconfiguring existing parts. Every choice carries sacrifice.

Example: A single suit of power armor refined over centuries. It flies, fights, stealths, and hacks, but only because function has been layered upon function. You cannot build a separate drone or weapon; everything must integrate into the suit. This limitation applies only when using this specific tinker power for creation. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

You are a Tinker who specializes in bees, not merely biological bees, but the concept of bees: swarms, hives, honey, and the intricate social machinery of collective industry. Your technology revolves around breeding, modifying, and directing insectoid creations toward any goal you can imagine. Your limitations as a tinker are slightly lifted. Examples:

>Custom Breeds: Engineer bees with specific behaviors: pollution eaters, target markers, programmable wax producers, or venom/healing deliverers.
>Hive Structures: Construct living hives that function as autonomous factories, refineries, or laboratories: processing ore, synthesizing pharmaceuticals, or generating alloys.
>Swarm Control: Direct thousands of individuals as a single coordinated intelligence for reconnaissance, construction, defense, or attack.
>Honey & Wax: Produce honey with programmable properties (supernutrients, preservatives, traps) and wax for self-repairing seals, programmable materials, or living memory storage.

You are a tinker capable of creating cutlery and dining implements of such exceptional quality they border on the supernatural. Your knives, forks, and spoons are perfectly balanced and can be crafted from innovative materials to perform specific and unorthodox tasks. While appearing mundane, a spoon from you can cool soup to the perfect temperature, and a fork can test for toxins. 

For combat, your creations are surprisingly effective: your throwing knives are able to return to your hand, fork tines can extend into fine-point grappling hooks, and a well-thrown dinner plate can be as accurate as a shuriken. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You understand the deepest secret of physics: symmetry is not a law, but a preference. Your specialty lies in instilling or breaking symmetries within physical systems to produce impossible phenomena. For instance, weaponization of magnetic monopoles is one of the practical application of this specialisation. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You perceive and manipulate reality below the Planck length, where space, time, and distance dissolve into continuous quantum foam. Where others see discrete components, you see flowing fields and transformations. You are terrible at counting or sorting, but unmatched at tracking and rewriting continuous processes. For example, you can build device to impose exotic spacetime metrics, like asymptotic barriers that make distance technically infinite. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You can construct devices that safely accelerate objects to near-light speeds and harness the exotic phenomena of relativistic motion. Examples include relativistic drive engines, solar-charged kinetic launchers (e.g., relativistic projectiles launchers), and systems that exploit time dilation or mass-energy effects. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You can build predictive psycho-social technologies that measure and forecast human intent, emotional state, and criminal probability. Your devices include cymatic scanners, stress-reactive drones, distributed social-hue monitors, and algorithmic judgment cores capable of flagging threats before they act. While highly effective at pacification and control, your tech is vulnerable to anomalous mental states or unpredictable outliers. But these always can captured and fed back into the system to include similiar cases and predict them better in the future. Your standard tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a Tinker specializing in acid-base chemistry, able to construct devices that manipulate pH across any medium: from pocket sprayers that instantly corrode alloys to handheld gel projectors that neutralize toxins mid-air. While you can craft battlefield-grade acids and bases, your true mastery lies in “pH-shifting”: tweaking the effective pH of materials and biological systems to force unexpected reactions: catalyzing explosions from inert compounds, paralyzing muscles via alkalosis, or dissolving non-metals with superacids (pH far below 0) and igniting organics with superbases (pH above 14). Your devices are precise, potent, and terrible when mixed carelessly. Your standard tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a tinker specializing in material fatigue, residual stress, and structural failure points. You can build devices that apply precisely tuned vibrational loads, thermal shocks, or micro-impacts to make practically any solid material (from steel to bone to even tinkertech alloys) crack, shatter, or deform along invisible fault lines. Your signature tech includes “pre-stress injectors” that leave materials seemingly intact but doomed to fail under the slightest pressure hours or days later. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a tinker focused on crystallography - specifically, the microscopic gaps between crystals in metals, ceramics, and even biological minerals (teeth, shells, kidney stones). You build “boundary probes” that slip between grains to weaken or reinforce structures at the atomic level. Your devices can embrittle a steel beam until it powders, or calcify a target’s joints into solid stone from the inside out. You excel at “seam bursting” - using fluid pressure or electrical charge to split materials cleanly along their natural grain lines. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a tinker specializing in systems that remember their past states: magnetic hysteresis, elastic hysteresis, even thermal or chemical lag. You build devices that exploit this memory to create “delayed effect traps” and “feedback loops.” A magnetic strip you create can be demagnetized but “remember” its orientation, snapping back violently hours later. A rubber cord you treat will stretch normally, then lock rigid when jerked. Your specialty is making materials lie about their present state, then punish anyone who trusts the lie. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a Tinker specializing in dentistry, oral biomechanics, and bio-mineralization. You can modify teeth, jaws, saliva, and cranial nerves: but crucially, you can also grow teeth outside your mouth or even detached from your body. These external “living tools” retain biological properties: razor-sharp enamel blades, gripping “tongue-hooks” for grapnel guns, crushing molars used as press-jaws, or self-repairing drill-burrs. Your implants deliver venom, sense chemicals, generate vibrations, or interface with your trigeminal nerve. Your spit transforms into adhesives, corrosives, or smoke via custom oral bacteria. Extracted teeth become disposable trackers or small explosives from your tinker work. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a Tinker specializing in liver and kidney biology: filtration, metabolism, and toxin processing. You build organic devices modeled on these organs: implants that scrub poisons from your own blood, external filter-glands that harvest or concentrate chemicals from any liquid, and hybrid liver-kidney growths that turn waste into weapons. Your “renal launcher” fires hyper-concentrated urea crystals; your “bile cutter” sprays digestive enzymes that liquefy steel. You survive any toxin by shunting it through wearable filter-bags. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a Tinker specializing in pharmaceuticals: drug design, delivery systems, and biological interactions. You create pills, patches, aerosols, implants, and injectables that produce effects ranging from subtle (pain suppression, sensory enhancement, metabolic acceleration) to extreme (instant paralysis, targeted cell death, temporary brain rewiring). Your signature is precision delivery: timed-release cascades, pH-triggered activation, or compounds that only activate in specific organs. You can produce antidotes on the fly, designer psychoactives for interrogation or control, and regeneration cocktails that close wounds in minutes. Your standard tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a Tinker specializing in precious metals: gold, silver, platinum, palladium, rhodium, and ruthenium. You can build almost any sci-fi or fantasy inspired device imaginable, but every creation must consist of at least 30% precious metals by composition. Each metal grants unique properties beyond their basic characteristics, when used for your tinkering. Now you just need to obtain these metals in needed amounts. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You are a Tinker specializing in psychiatry: neural interfaces, psychopharmacology, and behavioral conditioning. You build devices that read, influence, or rewrite mental states: headsets that suppress phobias, implants that block intrusive thoughts, wands that deliver targeted electromagnetic pulses to disrupt panic attacks or trigger euphoria. Your “mood regulators” release precisely timed neurotransmitter cocktails. Your “dream editors” record and rescript nightmares during sleep. Your most invasive work uses conditioned response loops: a small wearable that pairs a specific tone with painless micro-shocks until the target flinches at any trigger sound you choose. You cannot read minds in any literal sense, but you can map emotional patterns, install compulsions, and erase memories with enough time and contact. Your standard tinker limitations are slightly lifted.

You are a Tinker specializing in wood material: its growth, treatment, and anomalous modification. You create devices and controlled conditions to cultivate wood with impossible properties: planks as durable as steel, splinters that detonate on impact, fibers that remember their shape and snap back into place. Through "alchemical" infusions and growth rituals, you can “enchant” wooden objects with one-use effects: a carved statue that screams when broken, an arrow that seeks the nearest heartbeat, a walking stick that Roots anyone it touches. Your focus is not flashy or powerful by tinker standards, but it requires only wood to function: common, accessible, and everywhere. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You can construct devices that breach the thermodynamic floor, reaching into “negative heat” - a regime below absolute zero where entropy inverts, particles exhibit negative mass behavior, and energy flows paradoxically. This enables the fabrication of exotic matter (e.g., negative-temperature superfluids, time-reversed crystals), sub-absolute refrigerators that “heat” by cooling, and transmutation engines that restructure matter through inverted phase transitions. Your creations violate conventional conservation laws in localized, repeatable ways, but tend to self-destruct if they ever return to positive Kelvin ranges. You suffer from standard tinker limitations.

You can build a limited class of hypercomputational devices: super-Turing machines that solve non-algorithmic problems. Each device is narrowly specialized (e.g., predicting a single chaotic system, deciding a specific undecidable proposition, or perfectly compressing one type of data). These machines are fragile, power-hungry, and cannot run general software, but they seamlessly interface with your other tech, accelerating research, optimizing designs, or bypassing impossible calculations. Your own creativity remains essential - the oracles answer only what you specifically ask, in ways you must learn to interpret. You suffer all usual tinker limitations.

Your specialty is Textiles - not mere clothing, but the engineering of fabric as a dynamic medium. You build looms, spindles, and thread-laying rigs capable of producing super-textiles with properties like extreme tensile strength, energy diffusion, or reactive shaping. Designing fashionable attire comes naturally as a side effect, but your true art lies in treating any cloth-like material as a structural and functional technology. Your tinker limitations are partially lifted.

Your tinker focus is on plasma generation, containment, and projection. You can build reactors, conduits, and emission arrays that harness superheated ionized matter: ranging from cutting tools and sustained energy arcs to short-range plasma bursts with exotic effects. Defensive applications include containment fields and heat-flare shrouds. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

column2: Lightning in a Bottle (Hyperspec x Mad Scientist)
column5:
The main stickler with this power is that you need to carry a large energy source, both a detriment and advantage; it accumulates charges which you can spend to boost your gear, or it can power items built from fields outside of your specialty, at a high cost. But it remains a big glowing weak point for enemies to go after.

Your specialty is Voltage. Electricity and magnetism are your playground, especially more power-hungry tech you make. Within these fields, as long as you have the requisite power supply, materials, and supplies, there isn't much you can't do. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You don't require usual resources, instead setting up a workstation or node that produces resources for building at a sure and steady rate. This negates the component of needing to get a funding and material stream, while emphasizing pacing out the tinkering. In a pinch, you can destroy the workstation to rush a job.

Your specialty is Alloys, with an emphasis on Material Synthesis, Fabrication, and Transmutation, a specialty dealing primarily with esoteric metamaterials, armor and armor plating, though other materials and compositions are available as well. Alloy specialty Tinkers seem initially predisposed to defense. Not the case. As an Alloy Tinker, you can touch upon the 'immovable object' or 'unstoppable force' archetypes, generally utilizing aspects of both as you branch out in your tinkerings. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are an Immolated Tinker. You build tinkertech that gets so deep into the field of specialty that reality and the rules of physics may break down. Oftentimes, this is in the interests of tinkering-managed breaker transformations, partial or total, but it can extend to specific deployments or environmental effects as well.

Your field of specialty is in Coding/Programming. You'll have access to some stations to set up in your workshop, but most of your tinkering and coding will be applied to a frame or armor you'll wear, with some options for grafts and implants. You have limited access to AI. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are a Weatherman Tinker. You're not limited to weather manipulation, but you tend to blanket-target areas with your megaprojects, granting yourself and a limited few immunity or ability to navigate what is inevitably a haphazard or chaotic bombardment or unpredictable hazard for others. Start out with a basic kit and a limited (a few rounds) deployment of the 'storm', and build a device to make it constant, 24/7, 365/year effect, and then scale it up in area.

Your specialty is Temporal energy/Time. Your storms are temporal hazards; age someone up a few years, trap someone in a loop temporarily, make them face hazardous doppelgangers, etc. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are an Implement Tinker. You have a single item they fixate on, with a wide assortment of augments and patterns they can plug into that item. They get no peripheral items, no bodysuits to wear, terminals to build, and only a few trinkets that specifically focus on repairing, charging up, or otherwise working with the item, but the ways they can customize their item are endless.

The item is a Medkit, with the specialty being Medical Technology. As long as you can fit it in the medkit, there isn't much you can't make as far as healing and medical technology goes. Comes with a minor thinker power that gives an instinctive knowledge of the human anatomy, broad medical knowledge, and how to apply it. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

column2: Barriers, Forcefields, Oh My… (Liberty x Architect)
column5:
You are an Atelier Tinker. You don't utilize conventional workshops, but instead bring your workshops to battlefields or missions. Conflating workshop with your megaproject, you can call down obelisks, spikes, or other fixtures that become a part of the local terrain, unfolding with any workshop elements and upgrades made to date. 

Ramping up to speed, the megaproject gets increasing functionality and scale round by round, up to a limit dependent on the progress on your project and previous successful deployments. Your more conventional weapons and utility devices are necessary to protect your deployments.

You specialize in Defense, nearly all forms of it. From forcefields to armored emplacements and self-constructed fortresses, to reactive defenses that trigger when struck or reflect projectiles back at your attackers, you best dominate the field with overwhelming defense. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are a Quality Hyperspecialist; You can't build a wide range of things and can't tap into other specialties, but the stuff you build is better. Comes in some subvarieties, like the Power Hyperspecialist, the Scale Hyperspecialist, and the Hard Hyperspecialist. Often the best in your specialty.

You specialize in Simulations, with an emphasis on Predictions. You can simulate past, present and future events, but you require data and an analysis of a person's mental state or their choices in order to determine the most likely scenarios that might happen if you plan on predicting a person's future/past/present and not the weather or something. While the main function of your specialty is predictions, you can also create simulated combat scenarios of an individual at the cost of more extensive analysis on your chosen target; Endbringers, The Triumvirate, whatever you choose to simulate, you can. But be weary, whether it's combat simulations or predictions, what you put in, is what you get in return; Garbage in, garbage out.

Your simulations can also become physical. Make minions based on the data you've collected on a cape, and suddenly you could have a pocket Alexandria. Create a room for training purposes that simulate any feasible scenario and conditions. The sky is the limit, provided you have the data for it. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are an Air Raid Tinker; a combat tinker with a long-ranged focus, you can utilize deployments from a distant megaproject to assist you in your endeavors. Marking out areas for exceptionally long-ranged bombardments, airstrikes, blasts of energy, projections, or other 'strikes', you can use the same time their enemies are scrambling for cover to get into position to lay down more fire or to limit enemy movements so they can't escape the next bombardment.

You specialize in Precision Weaponry. You specialize in weapons that hit exactly what they are meant to hit, exactly when they are meant to hit it, from exactly the angle required to matter. Your weapons calculate, adjust, correct, and prosecute a target with obsessive focus. They do not merely fire at a person; they fire at the exposed servo joint in their armor, the weak spot in a shield rotation, the ankle as they dodge, the hand holding a detonator, the trigger mechanism of a gun, the tire axle of a getaway vehicle, or the three-millimeter gap between two hostages.

At the lower end, this means smart ammunition, assisted targeting systems, stabilized sniper platforms, trajectory-correcting bullets, and HUD-linked weak-point analysis. At the high end, this means practically undodgeable deployments of weaponry. You have all the usual tinker limitations.

You are a tinker specializing in high-energy phenomena and machinery. Your creations are universally power-hungry, energy-intense, and anything but subtle: a plasma pistol becomes a cannon, a bomb becomes a mini-nuke, and you simply cannot produce devices that operate below a certain threshold of energy output. You possess the full breadth of a tinker's capabilities, including the accompanying limitations.

You are a tinker specializing in the creation and application of designer hormones capable of manipulating physical appearance, physiology, and psychology with precision that borders on the supernatural. Any effect theoretically achievable through advanced targeted hormonal therapy is within your reach, but amplified far beyond natural extremes: reshaping bodies, rewriting metabolic processes, or recalibrating emotional responses with a single tailored dose. Your tinker limitations are slightly eased.

You are a tinker with an atypical focus: rather than building from your own specialty, your power lets you research and reverse-engineer other tinkertech devices, blueprints, or even incomprehensible alien technology, producing weaker, simpler, but mass-producible and fully understandable versions. These reproductions operate on principles that conventional science can grasp, making them reliable, maintainable, and replicable by mundane manufacturing. You suffer almost none of the usual tinker limitations - your only constraints involve the specialized tools and diagnostic devices required to properly analyze and deconstruct other tinkertech projects in the first place.
